I am an old man now, 80 years, but I still walk my plot and tell my sons and grandsons what to do. This beans plot I intercrop like always — cowpea with some sorghum and millet between, the way my father did and the way I have done for more than sixty seasons. Beans do not need much fertilizer like maize does; they feed themselves from the soil if you leave them. I will put a small amount of NPK at planting because the land has been worked too many years and the yields are not what they used to be, but I will not waste money on urea for cowpea — that is for the cereals. Spraying against the pod borers and the thrips is the one thing I cannot skip, otherwise the cowpea pods come out empty. My sons and their wives do most of the work now, and at weeding and harvest I pay a few young men from the village to help.
